summary.title: How to Build Your First Slack Bot with Python
summary.one_liner: You learn to create a basic Slack bot in Python using the slackclient library, a Slack App bot token, and the RTM API to read and reply to mentions.
keywords: how to make a slack bot
takeaways: Create a virtualenv, install slackclient==1.3.2, and create a Slack App with a bot user.
Store the bot user OAuth token in the SLACK_BOT_TOKEN environment variable and install the app to a development workspace.
Use the RTM API to read events in a loop, filter message events, and detect direct mentions of the bot with a regex.
Reply to commands by calling the chat.postMessage Web API method, and extend handle_command() with new commands.
Fix the websocket CA certificate error by downgrading websocket-client to 0.47.0 or setting WEBSOCKET_CLIENT_CA_BUNDLE.
summary.summary: The post, by Matt Makai and updated in December 2017, walks through building a simple Slack bot called StarterBot. It covers setting up a Python virtualenv, installing the slackclient library, creating a Slack App with a bot user, and exporting the bot token as an environment variable. The full starterbot.py is built step by step, with functions to parse events, detect mentions, and handle commands. The code is MIT-licensed in a public repository, and the post ends with a note on an SSL certificate issue and ideas for extending the bot.
